I have noticed when submitting that the new submission will only be at the top if I sort by new, something most casual users do not do. I think it would make sense if new submissions were featured near the top of hot as well, at least for a short time. So my suggestion is to adjust the algorithm to weigh time very heavily and taper off quickly to approach it's current state. I think this is contributing heavily to the perception that voat has very little activity.
New submissions are not featured prominently enough. Change the algorithm.

I totally agree. The problem is, currently, a post has to have a certain amount of upvoats before it starts to feature on the first pages, and it has to gain them fast. Upvoats take a while to get and so it takes around 1 to 4 hours for a post to reach this balance, and so the front page of Voat gets inundated with posts of that age. The worst part is they will stick around for a couple of hours after this balance is got, and new posts join to queue for hours.

A possible solution is simply to put some faith in new posts and put some on the front pages without having to reach loads of upvoats. The problem is then that you could end up with some poor quality posts for a front page.

Another possible solution is to put some faith into new posts that are posted by credible/known-to-be-good posters and front-page them early.

Or... Just go to new.

It takes at least one upvote to move out of new and be eligible for hot. So the more people who browse new, the more links make it to hot. Also, unlike reddit, new is actually really good here, so it's worth visiting.
I would rather have there be an account setting to set the default view for the front page. I generally always check out newer submissions first and would like that to be the default.

Here is how submissions are currently ranked:

 public static double CalculateNewRank(double currentRank, double submissionAge, double score)
 {
 const double penalty = 1;

 var newRank = (Math.Pow((score - 1), 0.8)) / (Math.Pow((submissionAge + 2), 1.8)) * penalty;

 return double.IsNaN(newRank) ? 0 : Math.Round(newRank, 7);
 }

To increase the weight of age we need to change the bit 

Math.Pow((submissionAge + 2), 1.8)

Either increase the sum or the power. Increasing the power from 1.8 to 1.95 has a dramatic effect on the result.
